subject.title: [Bug]: iOS app fails to connect over Tailscale CGNAT (100.x.x.x) — wss:// required but WebSocket upgrade silently dropped

question: What security posture should iOS support for Tailnet Gateway pairing: secure Serve/native TLS only, an explicit plaintext Tailnet opt-in, or documentation that direct Tailnet bind is not supported by iOS?
rationale: The remaining fix changes the TLS-versus-plaintext boundary for native mobile pairing and could affect Gateway auth, device bootstrap, and Tailscale deployment guidance.

options.title: Keep Secure Serve/TLS Path
options.body: Keep Tailnet CGNAT plaintext fail-closed, make Serve/native TLS pairing work with actionable iOS diagnostics, and document direct Tailnet bind as non-iOS unless TLS is configured.

options.title: Add Explicit Plaintext Tailnet Opt-In
options.body: Allow direct Tailnet ws:// only behind a visible operator/user opt-in and regression tests that preserve public-host fail-closed behavior.

options.title: Document Unsupported Direct CGNAT
options.body: Treat direct Tailnet bind as a CLI/browser path only and route iOS users to Tailscale Serve/Funnel or a public/private wss:// reverse proxy.

recommendation.title: Keep Secure Serve/TLS Path
recommendation.body: Keep Tailnet CGNAT plaintext fail-closed, make Serve/native TLS pairing work with actionable iOS diagnostics, and document direct Tailnet bind as non-iOS unless TLS is configured.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main Tailnet route advertising and setup-code history make this the closest current owner for the security/product direction.
